thread:
Connor O'Brien: heads up: we need a hotfix publish path for a customer-visible changelog correction today. The "nova-2-chat" entry we published this morning says "sunset in 30 days" but policy-approved timeline is 90 days. Support already has a ping from an enterprise admin.

Connor O'Brien: requirement: do NOT edit history in place. needs to preserve audit trail / immutability. what’s the correct procedure w/ the new draft->in_review->published flow?

ReleaseBot: :rotating_light: Release window status: freeze in effect for control-plane deploys until 18:00 PT. Docs publish jobs allowed with approval.

Michael Nguyen: yep, we can’t mutate a published entry. the generator has the supersede flow from PR-19018 ("rollback for published changelog entries"), but we haven’t used it in prod yet.

Michael Nguyen: mechanics as implemented:
- create a new entry with `type=correction` and `supersedes_entry_id=<old>`
- old entry gets `status=superseded` (still readable)
- feed emits both; clients can choose to hide superseded
- audit log records both the publish action + the supersede link

Jada Williams: +1. hotfix path should be: manual draft (not generator) -> expedited review -> publish correction. generator can be bypassed but we still have to go through approvals + RBAC.

Connor O'Brien: who can actually hit the publish endpoint on a correction right now? I have `release_engineering` role but I’m not sure if that includes emergency publish.

Jordan Lee: RBAC check: `release_engineering` can move `draft -> in_review`. publish requires `changelog_publisher` OR `emergency_publisher`.

Jordan Lee: Connor you don’t have `emergency_publisher` in prod (by design). we can grant a temporary timeboxed elevation via oncall security if needed, but preferred path is have an existing publisher do it.

Chloe Martin: I have `changelog_publisher` in staging + prod (needed for Console beta testing). can take publish action if we have final wording.

Dev Patel: support context: the issue is the customer-safe summary line + the "Deprecation timeline" section. they’re quoting 30 days verbatim. we should correct the wording and explicitly say "no action required until <date>".

Elliot Price: on docs side: publishing a new entry will create a new permalink for that entry. question: do we want the original URL to remain valid and show "corrected" banner? (that’s what docs PR-982 behavior does: superseded entry stays but shows a warning at top and links to correction.)

Michael Nguyen: correct. the old page persists, but the banner is driven off the `status=superseded` + `superseded_by_entry_id` fields.

Connor O'Brien: ok, proposed plan:
1) create correction entry that supersedes the published one
2) publish correction (no edits to original)
3) validate: console shows correction as most recent, old entry flagged as superseded
4) confirm RSS/JSON feed has both + correct ordering
5) notify support + affected account

Connor O'Brien: can we do this without a control-plane deploy? (freeze)

Michael Nguyen: yes. publish is a normal API call; no deploy needed. docs publish job is triggered automatically off publish event.

Jada Williams: approval workflow: we still need a reviewer signoff. for hotfix, requirement is 1 product reviewer + 1 release engineer, but can be async within 30 mins.

Connor O'Brien: Marissa is in meetings. can we use Paula as product reviewer for this? it’s deprecation language.

Jada Williams: yes, Paula has `release_notes_product_reviewer`.

Jordan Lee: also looping in Kevin for audit language. we should ensure we capture:
- actor (publisher)
- reviewer(s)
- reason="customer-visible correction"
- link to incident/support ticket id

Kevin Osei: +1. please include the reason + reference ID in the publish metadata. For audit, we need the supersede relationship immutable and the original content hash retained.

Kevin Osei: also: do NOT hard-delete the old feed item. some customers ingest and store it; the correction must be additive.

Elliot Price: wording suggestion (docs style guide compliant):
"Correction (2024-01-30): The prior entry incorrectly stated a 30-day deprecation window. The deprecation timeline is 90 days from announcement. No changes are required until 2024-04-29."

Dev Patel: looks good. add "If you have pinned versions, your existing pin will continue to resolve." (customers keep asking.)

Chloe Martin: I can draft the correction in the admin UI now. need exact fields:
- impacted deployments (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
- compatibility note
- deprecation timeline section

Michael Nguyen: for impacted deployments, set Hosted + Dedicated. Private is "depends on customer-managed" so we usually say "Private deployments are not automatically updated".

Connor O'Brien: can we paste the exact correction body here so Paula can approve in-thread?

Chloe Martin: draft text below (customer-safe):
---
Impact: Corrects the previously published deprecation timeline for `nova-2-chat`.
What changed: The 2024-01-30 entry incorrectly stated a 30-day window. The correct timeline is 90 days from announcement.
Compatibility: No API changes. Existing pinned model versions continue to resolve as-is.
Deprecation timeline: Deprecation will occur no earlier than 2024-04-29. We will provide at least 90 days notice prior to any removal.
More info: See Console > Model catalog > `nova-2-chat` > Changelog.
---

Connor O'Brien: looks aligned. tagging @Paula Mendes for quick approval.

Jada Williams: make sure the entry type is "correction" not "deprecation" or it’ll trip the template taxonomy checks.

Jordan Lee: and set `public_summary` <= 280 chars; feed uses it as preview.

Kevin Osei: plus include reference: "SUP-18502" (or whatever the support ticket is) in internal-only metadata; should not leak in public fields.

Dev Patel: support ticket is SUP-18502 (confusing wording) + we also have SUP-18421 asking about immutability. Use SUP-18502 as the correction reference.

Elliot Price: reminder: don’t mention internal model nicknames / vendor. keep to public model id.

Connor O'Brien: (reactions: Chloe Martin :thumbsup:, Michael Nguyen :+1:, Kevin Osei :+1:)

Chloe Martin: Paula approved in DM (can screenshot if needed). I’ll proceed with publish.

ReleaseBot: ChangeLog Publish Event (pending): entry_id=clg_01HPYQZ3K4J8A2, action=publish, requested_by=chloe.martin

Chloe Martin: published. correction entry_id `clg_01HPYQZ3K4J8A2` supersedes `clg_01HPYQJ9T7M1FQ`.

Michael Nguyen: checking feed… JSON endpoint shows both, new one sorted above old by published_at. old entry has `status=superseded` and `superseded_by=clg_01HPYQZ3K4J8A2`.

Elliot Price: docs job triggered. should be live in ~5-10 mins. I’ll verify banners + links.

Kevin Osei: audit log: I see two events:
- `model_changelog.published` actor=chloe.martin reviewers=[paula.mendes, connor.obrien] reason="customer-visible correction" ref="SUP-18502"
- `model_changelog.superseded` linking old->new
Looks good.

Connor O'Brien: awesome. Dev can you notify the support thread + customer-facing guidance? ("correction published, link stable")

Dev Patel: will do. we’ll reply to SUP-18502 with the new entry link and note that original remains accessible for audit.

Elliot Price: docs link is live and shows "This entry has been superseded" banner on the old page, linking to the correction. :white_check_mark:

Connor O'Brien: thanks all. follow-up: we should document this hotfix path in the operator how-to + add a quick checklist for freeze windows. I’ll open a Linear subtask off ENG-4926.

Michael Nguyen: pls also add a guardrail: if deprecation window is < policy min, template should warn before publish. could’ve caught the 30 vs 90.

Jada Williams: +1. I’ll capture as workflow requirement (pre-publish validation step) and route to Quentin/Michael.

Connor O'Brien: closing the loop here. great save.
